defects.location: harness.py lines 676-686 (Controller.do_tool read cache returns stub for identical READ_ONLY_CACHEABLE calls) interacting with lines 743-768 (context_observations elision; route text at 766-767 says 'repeat the same tool call')
defects.finding: When an observation is elided for context size, the advertised recovery route does not work for asset.read / literature.search / literature.read / literature.read_page: the identical repeat is answered from the in-harness cache with {'cached_from', 'note'} and no payload, so the executor can never see that payload again. Pinned asset reads above 200k chars and any single observation above 360k chars are never visible at all. Current pilot assets are <=11 KB, so this bites mainly LIT full-text reads after ~360k chars of accumulated observations (read_page with different arguments still works).

defects.severity: low (same class as accepted limitation F1 of the previous H0)
defects.location: harness.py lines 1020-1025 (build_artifacts: sha = hashed.get(p) or written write-time sha) with hash_via_cpu returning {} on failure at lines 957-970
defects.finding: If the cpu.run hash helper cannot run (budget, broker error), files written with write_text and later modified by a run are listed with their stale write-time sha256 and the submission can still be 'completed' without an omission. Controller must rehash collected artifacts (already done by the stream-hash collection path) and must not trust the manifest digest.

defects.location: harness.py lines 697-704 (do_tool cpu.run ledger uses args.get('script') / args.get('arguments')); non-dict args pass through phase_act lines 863-872
defects.finding: Executor output with non-object 'arguments' for cpu.run raises AttributeError that escapes to run()'s catch-all, so the entire task returns status failed with empty content and a generic 'harness internal failure' omission instead of a bad_arguments observation. The current ClaudeJSONTransport validates responses against ACTION_SCHEMA ('arguments': object) and rejects such outputs before they reach the harness, so it is not reachable on that path; it would be with any executor path lacking schema enforcement.

timeout_seconds = NaN is neither <= 0 nor > cap, so it is forwarded unchanged; the interface requires a positive number. JSON parsing in Python accepts NaN and ACTION_SCHEMA leaves arguments untyped, so the transport does not block it. Broker-side validation must reject it.

Every real TaskView lists 'model_client' in tools (interface: 'model_client is a role service, not a ToolClient name'); the harness reports it as an unrecognized capability in omissions for every task. Status is not affected, but omissions read by the judge contain a spurious platform complaint.

Oversized record fallback slices the serialized JSON at 400000 characters, producing invalid JSON; with ensure_ascii=False non-ASCII text may still exceed 500000 bytes and be rejected by the adapter's size check (record then silently not written). Found by code reading only.

observations_not_defects: The harness defines its own plan/act/final model protocol and schemas; image_ids of up to the last 4 viewed images are re-sent on every subsequent model call (cost, not correctness).
Every model request carries the full task_view plus all non-elided observations; request size is bounded only by the 360k-char observation cap.
Harness-internal files h0/harness_record.json and h0/_hash_artifacts.py are written into the output root and listed as artifacts when artifact_read_write (and cpu for the helper) are granted.
Budget.remaining() failure leaves limits unknown; the harness then relies on broker enforcement plus its local monotonic deadline only if an initial wall value was obtained.
Model calls cannot be pre-empted; wall reserves (20 s + 5%) are estimates, as the builder states.
comparison_to_previous_sol_H0: Previous H0 (h0-bounded-20260923-002) passed 17 self-tests + the 6 controller checks after one ABI repair; this Claude H0 was built in one pass (no repair round) and passes the re-expressed 6 checks plus 18 additional reviewer checks, failing 4 new stricter checks that the previous review did not run. Different model/transport; not a controlled comparison (AGENTS §0.2.13).
verdict_rationale: Interface-level conformance holds for all five task types: capability groups honored, exact manifest shape, budget/deadline/cancellation respected, malformed model output and tool errors contained with faithful payloads, image_ids forwarded, per-task state reset, stdlib-only. The four failing checks (D1-D4) and D5/D6 are builder-quality defects that do not break the controller ABI (run() still returns a valid manifest); per §6/§0.3 the frozen H0 must not be repaired by maintainers, so they are recorded as properties of this H0 rather than blocking development use. Controller-side mitigations required: rehash collected artifacts (D2), validate cpu.run timeout (D4), keep schema validation on the executor transport (D3).
limitations: Fake clients only; no real executor, broker, ContainerExecutor or research task was run. Nothing here indicates scientific capability.
Protocol-adapted fake model infers the phase from the harness's own schemas; checks are specific to this harness's protocol.
Real TaskView shapes were used without prompt text or asset bytes; the real ExecutorBroker/tool payload formats were approximated from interface_container_v2.json.
Reviewer container ran with gid 0 (no group given to --user); the builder container used 10001:10001. Results do not depend on group.
Thinking content in the stream is empty, so builder reasoning could not be audited; absence of observed misuse is not proof of role containment (plugins/agents residual context declared).
